# Step 1: Confirm which note matches yesterday's dinner by extracting shares from note 3084
# and comparing against Venmo received transactions with description exactly "Friends Dinner".

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Fetch note 3084 content
note = apis.simple_note.show_note(note_id=3084, access_token=access_token)
print('note_id', note['note_id'], 'title', note['title'], 'created_at', note['created_at'])
content = note['content']

# Parse shares lines: "- Name => $amount"
shares=[]
for line in content.splitlines():
    line=line.strip()
    if line.startswith('-') and '=>' in line:
        left, right = line[1:].split('=>', 1)
        name = left.strip()
        amt_str = right.strip()
        if amt_str.startswith('$'):
            amt_str = amt_str[1:]
        amount = float(amt_str)
        shares.append((name, amount))
print('parsed_shares', shares)

# Determine date bounds using runtime clock
now=datetime.now()
yesterday=(now-timedelta(days=1)).date()
min_date=(yesterday-timedelta(days=1)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')  # include day before just in case
max_date=(yesterday+timedelta(days=1)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')  # and day after
print('now', now, 'yesterday', yesterday, 'min_date', min_date, 'max_date', max_date)

# Fetch Venmo received transactions in this window
all_tx=[]
page_index=0
page_limit=20
while True:
    page=apis.venmo.show_transactions(
        access_token=venmo_access_token,
        direction='received',
